findings.issue: After rebuilding, verified against a stale manually-started server and a cache-tainted agent-browser session, then spent ~8 turns debugging a hydration 'bug' that didn't exist (three discarded hypotheses: stale build, SSR select quirk, broken hydration) before realizing the browser had cached pre-fix assets.
findings.suggestion: Make 'restart server + fresh browser session after every rebuild' a standing step before browser-based verification; a 404 on a modulepreload asset should immediately point to stale cache.

findings.issue: Ran 'agent-browser screenshot /tmp/shot-home.png --full-page' which misparsed the flag and wrote a file named '--full-page'; two turns spent locating it.
findings.suggestion: Read the CLI's flag syntax (agent-browser skills get core) before using advanced flags, or place flags before the path.

findings.issue: pkill -f patterns matched the calling bash process itself, killing its own shell (exit 143) and forcing a retry turn.
findings.suggestion: Use a more specific pattern (e.g. pkill -f 'node .output/server/index.mjs$') or track PIDs at start time.

findings.issue: Three web_fetch calls to docs.solidjs.com v2 paths 404'd before switching to curl and the official GitHub templates.
findings.suggestion: When a docs site's URL scheme is unknown, discover link structure once (curl the getting-started page for hrefs) instead of guessing section URLs.

findings.issue: Used window._$HY and script-tag probing to guess at hydration status instead of immediately checking the network log that revealed the stale-asset 404.
findings.suggestion: Check console/network errors first when a client-rendered state looks wrong after a rebuild.

summary: A disciplined, well-planned session: thorough up-front research (including correctly discovering SolidStart 2.x as the current stable), a single-pass implementation, and one-shot diagnosis of the only real test failures. Verification was exemplary — full suite after the last edit plus visual comparison against every reference screenshot at both breakpoints. The one blemish is a self-inflicted ~8-turn detour chasing a phantom bug caused by its own stale server/browser state.
